rules.title: MFA Failure Burst
rules.description: Detects a burst of 5 or more failed authentication or MFA events for the same actor within a correlation window. Indicates brute force or credential spray activity.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate users forgetting passwords; locked accounts generating repeated failure events; automated health checks with stale credentials.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor for known service accounts with documented rotation delays. Set expiry â‰¤ 30 days.

rules.title: Failed Login Across Multiple Services
rules.description: Detects 4 or more failed logins for the same actor spanning 2 or more services. Cross-service failures indicate credential spray targeting multiple SaaS/SSO endpoints.
rules.false_positive_notes: SSO misconfiguration causing failures across multiple integrated apps; users switching devices while sessions are cached.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor for known automation accounts. Review SSO error logs for systematic causes before suppressing.

rules.title: Successful Login from High-Risk IP
rules.description: Detects a successful authentication where the source IP carries a risk score â‰¥ 0.70. Indicates login from a known suspicious or anomalous location.
rules.false_positive_notes: VPN exit nodes with high community risk scores used by legitimate employees; travel to regions with shared high-risk IP ranges.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + source_ip for documented corporate VPN exit nodes. Add source IP to allowlist at the feed level where possible.

rules.title: Impossible Travel â€” Multiple Source IPs
rules.description: Detects successful logins for the same actor from 2 or more distinct source IPs within a correlation window. Suggests concurrent session from different locations or credential sharing.
rules.false_positive_notes: Corporate NAT or load balancers presenting different external IPs for the same user; mobile + desktop simultaneous sessions from different network paths.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor for users with documented split-tunneling or multi-device workflows. Review NAT topology before suppression.

rules.title: Identity Privilege Escalation
rules.description: Detects privilege escalation events for an actor â€” role assignment, admin action, or privilege-modifying event types in identity telemetry.
rules.false_positive_notes: Scheduled IAM role rotations; onboarding workflows that temporarily elevate privileges; infrastructure-as-code automation granting/removing roles programmatically.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + event_type for documented CI/CD service accounts. Require ticket reference for any suppression > 7 days.

rules.title: Unusual Login Source â€” Multiple Actors
rules.description: Detects 3 or more distinct users authenticating from the same source IP within a correlation window. Indicates credential spray from a shared attack infrastructure.
rules.false_positive_notes: Shared office NAT or proxy IP presenting many users; kiosk environments; corporate VPN concentrator.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by source_ip for known corporate NAT/VPN egress IPs. Document in suppression registry with network team sign-off.

rules.title: Unusual Cloud API Activity
rules.description: Detects 3 or more high-risk cloud API events (risk_score â‰¥ 0.70) for the same actor within a correlation window.
rules.false_positive_notes: Security scanning tools; automated compliance checks; legitimate high-volume API integrations with elevated risk scores due to call volume.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + cloud_account for known scanning service accounts. Validate risk score source before suppressing.

rules.title: Suspicious Cloud Object Access
rules.description: Detects 5 or more cloud object storage accesses (GetObject, ListObject, etc.) by the same actor within a correlation window. Indicates potential data staging or reconnaissance.
rules.false_positive_notes: Application backup jobs; data analytics pipelines accessing objects in bulk; media streaming services.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + cloud_account for documented data pipeline service accounts. Threshold may be raised for high-volume environments.

rules.title: Cloud Mass Download
rules.description: Detects 10 or more download events by the same actor within a correlation window. Indicates potential data exfiltration via cloud storage.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate bulk data exports for analytics; developer downloading dataset for local development; authorized data migration.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + cloud_account with ticket reference. Threshold configurable via XDR_CORRELATION_MASS_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD env var (future).

rules.title: New Cloud Access Key Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a new cloud access key or API credential. Access key creation is a common persistence and privilege escalation step.
rules.false_positive_notes: Onboarding new service accounts; automated key rotation pipelines; infrastructure provisioning via IaC.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + cloud_account for documented key rotation automation. Require change ticket reference.

rules.title: Cloud Security Setting Modified
rules.description: Detects modification of cloud security settings â€” IAM policies, security group rules, bucket ACLs, or logging configurations. Defense evasion and persistence indicator.
rules.false_positive_notes: Security team applying policy updates; IaC pipeline managing security group rules; compliance automation.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor + cloud_account for security team automation accounts. Review policy changes are in approved change window.

rules.title: Unusual SaaS Admin Activity
rules.description: Detects administrative actions in SaaS applications by the same actor. Administrative actions on SaaS platforms are a common target for account takeover.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate SaaS administrators performing routine management; IT helpdesk with elevated SaaS roles.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by actor for documented SaaS admin accounts. Scope suppression narrowly â€” admin actions are high-value signals.

rules.title: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Relationship
rules.description: Detects when a suspicious child process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, etc.) is spawned by an unexpected parent associated with office or productivity applications. Detected via within-batch pid/ppid correlation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate macro-enabled documents in automation workflows; IT admin scripts invoked from Outlook rules; document conversion pipelines using Office COM automation.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process.name + process.hash for signed corporate tooling. Never suppress by process name alone.

rules.title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
rules.description: Detects PowerShell launched with an encoded command argument (-enc, -e, -EncodedCommand). Encoding is frequently used to obfuscate malicious payloads from command-line logging.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate automation scripts using encoded commands for special character handling; deployment tools (SCCM, Ansible) that encode commands for transport.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process.hash for known signed deployment tools. Never suppress by process name alone.

rules.title: Executable Written to Temporary Directory
rules.description: Detects executable or script files written to temporary directories. Threat actors frequently stage payloads in Temp directories before execution.
rules.false_positive_notes: Software installers legitimately extracting to Temp before installation; browser downloads to Temp before user action; update mechanisms staging updates.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process.hash for known installer binaries. Suppress by file.path pattern for specific vendor staging directories.

rules.title: Failed Login Burst (Endpoint)
rules.description: Detects 3 or more failed login or MFA failures for the same user on the same host within a single correlation window. Endpoint-sourced login events distinct from identity/SSO telemetry.
rules.false_positive_notes: Users mistyping passwords; locked accounts generating repeated failure events; automated health checks with expired credentials.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + user for service accounts with documented rotation delays. Threshold is configurable in the rule implementation.

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query
rules.description: Detects DNS queries exhibiting DGA-like characteristics: domain length > 40 characters, or digit density > 40%. Heuristic â€” not a threat intelligence match.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate CDN and cloud service domains with long names; GUID-based service endpoints; telemetry and crash-reporting domains with high numeric density.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + dns.domain for known-legitimate long domains. Add to domain allowlist at the feed level where possible.

rules.title: Suspicious Outbound Network Connection
rules.description: Detects outbound connections from an endpoint to an external (non-RFC1918) IP on a non-standard port. Common C2 communication pattern.
rules.false_positive_notes: Custom application ports; gaming or VoIP applications; peer-to-peer applications; developer tools on non-standard ports.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + destination_ip + destination_port for known application endpoints. Add port to the common port allowlist for organization-wide exceptions.

rules.title: Endpoint IOC IP Match
rules.description: Endpoint network event (source_ip or destination_ip) matches an active, non-expired IOC of type 'ip' in the threat intelligence store. Severity and confidence inherit from the matched IOC.
rules.false_positive_notes: IOC feed false positives; shared IP ranges where only some hosts are malicious; expired threat intel still in feed.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by ioc_id for known false-positive IOC entries. Deactivate the IOC in the store (active=false) rather than suppressing at the rule level where possible.

rules.title: Endpoint IOC Domain Match
rules.description: Endpoint DNS query matches an active, non-expired IOC of type 'domain' in the threat intelligence store. Severity and confidence inherit from the matched IOC.
rules.false_positive_notes: Domain in IOC feed that has been sinkholed or taken down; legitimate service sharing domain with malicious subdomain.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by ioc_id for sinkholed or reclaimed domains. Update IOC active=false in the store for decommissioned threats.

rules.title: Endpoint IOC File Hash Match
rules.description: Endpoint process or file write event carries a SHA-256 hash matching an active, non-expired IOC of type 'file_hash' in the threat intelligence store. Severity and confidence inherit from the matched IOC.
rules.false_positive_notes: Hash collision in feed (very rare for SHA-256); legitimate tool flagged by community feed due to dual-use nature.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by ioc_id for confirmed false-positive hashes. Remove from IOC store or set active=false. Do not suppress at rule level for hash-based rules â€” hash matches are almost always significant.

rules.title: Scheduled Task Persistence
rules.description: Detects creation or modification of a scheduled task via schtasks.exe or a scheduled_task_create endpoint event. Scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism used by attackers to survive reboots.
rules.false_positive_notes: Software installers registering legitimate update tasks; IT automation tools creating maintenance schedules; Group Policy applying scheduled task policies.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + scheduled_task.name for known-legitimate automation accounts. Require change ticket reference for suppressions > 7 days.

rules.title: New Service Installed
rules.description: Detects installation of a new Windows service via sc.exe create or a service_install endpoint event. Attacker-installed services commonly point to executables in non-standard paths (Temp, AppData) and run as SYSTEM.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate software installers; IT management tools (SCCM, Ansible, PDQ) deploying services; infrastructure-as-code provisioning new system services.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + service.name for known-legitimate service deployments. Require change management ticket for any suppression.

rules.title: Possible C2 Beacon Pattern
rules.description: Detects 3 or more outbound network connections from the same endpoint to the same external IP and port within a single correlation window. Periodic repetitive connections to non-standard external ports are a common C2 beaconing pattern.
rules.false_positive_notes: Long-running application sessions maintaining persistent connections; heartbeat protocols to cloud services on custom ports; monitoring agents polling remote collectors.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + destination_ip + destination_port for known-legitimate application endpoints. Add to common port allowlist for organization-wide exceptions.

rules.title: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Chain (Behavioral)
rules.description: Detects shell or interpreter processes spawned from unexpected parent processes on Linux endpoints. Covers bash/sh/python/perl spawned by web servers, databases, or other non-interactive parent processes. Indicates possible remote code execution or webshell activity.
rules.false_positive_notes: Administrative scripts run from web management consoles; deployment pipelines executing via application processes; legitimate shell wrappers in managed runtimes.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + parent_process for known-legitimate management processes. Require approval for suppressions involving web server processes (nginx, apache, gunicorn).

rules.title: Suspicious Shell-to-Shell Execution Chain
rules.description: Detects multi-hop shell chains where an interpreter process (bash, sh, python, perl) spawns another shell or interpreter. Typical pattern in exploitation and lateral movement: initial RCE spawns shell which spawns another shell to establish a more stable session.
rules.false_positive_notes: Shell scripts that source other scripts; interactive terminals within containers; development environments with nested REPLs; CI runners executing multi-stage scripts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process_name + parent_name pair for known-legitimate shell chaining patterns. Validate against build pipelines before suppressing.

rules.title: Suspicious Long-Lived Interactive Process
rules.description: Detects interactive shell or interpreter processes that have been running for more than 1 hour. Long-lived interactive sessions are anomalous for short-lived automation tasks and may indicate a persistent reverse shell or attacker dwell-time activity.
rules.false_positive_notes: Analyst SSH sessions; persistent background services implemented as shell scripts; long-running Python daemons; administrative screen/tmux sessions.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + user for known administrator accounts. Suppress by process.name for known long-running daemon processes. Threshold of 1 hour is configurable.

rules.title: New or Unexpected Persistence Entry
rules.description: Detects new or previously-unseen persistence mechanisms on a Linux endpoint: new systemd service files, new crontab entries, or new startup script modifications. New persistence items that do not match known-good inventory baselines may indicate attacker persistence installation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Package manager installations adding systemd services; IT automation tools creating cron jobs; application updates registering new services; configuration management applying baseline.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + item_key for known-legitimate package-managed services. Require change ticket reference for manual suppression of persistence items added outside scheduled maintenance windows.

rules.title: Suspicious Process Execution Chain
rules.description: Detects multi-hop shell execution chains where a shell process ancestry includes downloaders (curl, wget) and outbound network connections. Patterns such as bashâ†’curlâ†’sh or pythonâ†’wgetâ†’bash indicate staged payload delivery or living-off-the-land exploitation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate automation scripts using curl/bash pipelines; package manager operations; CI/CD pipeline stages running shell commands.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + chain root process for known-legitimate automation. Require change ticket for suppressions involving web server parent processes.

rules.title: Suspicious Beacon-like Outbound Pattern
rules.description: Detects repetitive outbound connections from the same process to the same destination IP and port, with high destination reuse score. Multi-snapshot temporal analysis identifies processes with 3 or more repeated connections suggesting C2 beaconing.
rules.false_positive_notes: Long-running application sessions; health check daemons; monitoring agents; sync services connecting to cloud endpoints on fixed intervals.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process + destination for known-legitimate persistent connections. Validate against application architecture docs before suppressing.

rules.title: Living-off-the-Land Binary (LOLBin) Usage
rules.description: Detects use of living-off-the-land binaries (curl, wget, bash, python, perl, nc, base64, systemctl) on the endpoint. LOLBin usage becomes more suspicious when combined with: outbound network connections, encoded command indicators (base64), or spawning from unexpected parent processes.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate system administration using curl/wget; Python scripts for data processing; bash scripts for automation; systemctl for service management during deployments.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + process + parent for known-legitimate administrative workflows. Base confidence on combination of indicators rather than single LOLBin presence.

rules.title: Persistence + Active Shell + Outbound Correlation
rules.description: Detects the behavioral combination of: (1) active persistence items on the host, (2) shell processes running concurrently, and (3) outbound network connections from those shell processes. This three-way correlation indicates a persistence mechanism that has established an active shell with command-and-control communication.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate monitoring agents with persistence (systemd) making health check connections; CI runners registered as services with outbound build connections; managed endpoints with authorised remote access services.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + persistence item for known-legitimate services with documented outbound connectivity requirements. Require security review for suppressions involving new or unrecognised persistence items.

rules.title: Rare Parent-Child Process Relationship
rules.description: Detects unusual parent-child process combinations with a rarity score. Specifically flags shell/interpreter processes spawned by web servers, databases, or application frameworks (nginx, apache, gunicorn, mysqld, postgres) which are unexpected in normal operation and strongly indicate exploitation such as web shell execution or remote code execution.
rules.false_positive_notes: Web application management interfaces legitimately invoking system commands; deployment scripts running via application process; development environments with embedded terminals.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + parent + child for known-legitimate management workflows. Database and web server parent suppressions require explicit security team sign-off. Threshold: rarity score >= 0.70.

rules.title: Repeated Behavioral Execution Chain Pattern
rules.description: Detects the same suspicious execution chain pattern (same process ancestry fingerprint) occurring multiple times across collection cycles. Repeated chains indicate persistent automation, scheduled tasks, or an attacker maintaining recurring access.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate scheduled jobs with consistent execution patterns; CI/CD pipeline stages; system services with periodic execution; health check scripts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + chain fingerprint for known-legitimate periodic processes. Threshold is configurable. Require change ticket for suppressions involving web server parent chains.

rules.title: Multi-Host Beacon Pattern to Same Destination
rules.description: Detects the same destination IP:port being targeted by beacon-like connection patterns across multiple hosts. Multi-host coordination to a single external destination strongly indicates a C2 server being contacted by multiple compromised endpoints.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate cloud service endpoints (telemetry, CDN, update servers) contacted by multiple hosts; corporate monitoring infrastructure; shared VPN gateways.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by destination IP + port for documented corporate infrastructure. Require threat intelligence review before suppressing previously unseen destinations with multi-host activity.

rules.title: Repeated LOLBin Execution Sequence
rules.description: Detects the same living-off-the-land binary executing with similar patterns across multiple collection cycles. A LOLBin that repeatedly executes (especially with outbound activity or encoded commands) suggests automated use by persistence mechanisms or C2 implants.
rules.false_positive_notes: System health check scripts executing on a schedule; legitimate backup tools; update managers using curl/wget periodically; monitoring agents using Python scripts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + LOLBin for known-legitimate scheduled executions. Require security review for suppressing LOLBins with base64-encoded arguments.

rules.title: Persistence Item Reactivation Pattern
rules.description: Detects a persistence item that was previously observed as 'new', disappeared from one snapshot, and reappeared in a subsequent snapshot. This reactivation pattern may indicate persistence that is being rotated or reinstalled by an attacker after partial detection or removal attempts.
rules.false_positive_notes: Services restarted after maintenance windows; package reinstallation from package manager; configuration management re-applying baseline after drift detection.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by host + item key for persistence items with documented reinstall procedures. Require change ticket for suppressions of items with no known reinstall reason.

rules.title: Identity Failure Followed by Endpoint Shell Execution
rules.description: Detects identity authentication failure for an actor followed by endpoint shell execution from the same user. Cross-domain advisory-only correlation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate users running shells after failed password attempts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known CI/CD actors with documented shell usage.

rules.title: Identity Privilege Escalation Correlated with Endpoint Persistence
rules.description: Detects identity privilege escalation correlated with new endpoint persistence entries from the same user. Advisory-only cross-domain shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate admin privilege changes with scheduled maintenance.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented maintenance windows.

rules.title: SaaS Activity Correlated with Endpoint Beacon Pattern
rules.description: Detects SaaS anomaly events from a source IP also observed initiating endpoint beacon patterns. Cross-domain advisory-only correlation.
rules.false_positive_notes: NAT or shared egress IPs; corporate proxies.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented shared NAT or proxy IPs.

rules.title: Multiple Hosts LOLBin Activity to Shared Destination
rules.description: Detects multiple endpoint hosts using LOLBin processes to connect to the same destination within the correlation window. Indicates possible lateral movement or coordinated C2.
rules.false_positive_notes: Update servers and monitoring agents using built-in OS tools.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known update/patch server IPs.

rules.title: Cross-Domain Attack Progression Detected
rules.description: Detects an actor appearing across multiple telemetry domains (identity, cloud, SaaS, endpoint) within the same correlation batch. Requires endpoint involvement plus at least one additional domain. Advisory-only cross-domain shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Power users with legitimate multi-domain activity; automation accounts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented service accounts with expected multi-domain access.

rules.title: Rapid Shell Chain Detected in Streaming Telemetry
rules.description: Detects three or more shell execution events from the same host within a single streaming batch. Indicates potential interactive attacker activity or automated shell chaining. Advisory-only streaming shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate admin shell sessions; automation scripts; deployment pipelines.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known admin hosts with documented interactive shell use.

rules.title: Rapid Persistence Creation Detected in Streaming Telemetry
rules.description: Detects three or more persistence item creation or modification events from the same host within a single streaming batch. Indicates potential persistence installation activity. Advisory-only streaming shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Software installers; OS updates; legitimate service registrations.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress during known maintenance windows and software deployments.

rules.title: Burst Outbound Connection Activity Detected in Streaming Telemetry
rules.description: Detects ten or more outbound connection events from the same host within a single streaming batch. Indicates potential data exfiltration, C2 beaconing, or scanning activity. Advisory-only streaming shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: CDN/cloud workloads with many legitimate outbound connections; patch management systems.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known high-volume hosts with documented outbound patterns.

rules.title: Short-Lived Suspicious Process Detected in Streaming Telemetry
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process that starts and terminates within the same streaming batch window. Indicates potential command-and-control callback or recon tool use. Advisory-only streaming shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Short-lived legitimate utilities; health checks; monitoring agents.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented short-lived processes with known legitimate purpose.

rules.title: Rapid Execution Beacon Pattern Detected in Streaming Telemetry
rules.description: Detects four or more process_started events for the same process name from the same host within a single streaming batch. Consistent execution count suggests automated beaconing behaviour. Advisory-only streaming shadow rule.
rules.false_positive_notes: Scheduled task runners; health-check scripts; monitoring agents with frequent execution.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented scheduled processes with known execution intervals.

rules.title: Suspicious DNS TLD Query Detected
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to known suspicious or high-risk top-level domains. Advisory-only network shadow rule. No active blocking.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate services using .xyz, .top, or other generic TLDs.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented business-approved domains on suspicious TLDs.

rules.title: Repeated DNS TXT Queries Detected
rules.description: Detects multiple DNS TXT record queries from the same host in a correlation window. TXT queries are commonly abused for DNS tunneling C2 communication. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: SPF/DKIM validation tools; DNS management scripts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented DNS administration hosts.

rules.title: Repeated NXDOMAIN Responses Detected
rules.description: Detects five or more NXDOMAIN responses to a single host in a correlation window. May indicate DGA domain generation activity or DNS-based command-and-control. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Misconfigured DNS resolvers; browsing to deleted sites; split-horizon DNS environments.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known misconfigured hosts with documented NX pattern.

rules.title: Suspicious Proxy User-Agent Detected
rules.description: Detects known tool or scanner user-agent strings in proxy telemetry. May indicate automated tooling, scanning, or malware. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate automation tools; developer testing tools; monitoring agents.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented automation hosts with known user-agent patterns.

rules.title: High Volume Proxy Egress Detected
rules.description: Detects hosts transferring more than 50 MiB outbound via proxy in a correlation window. May indicate data exfiltration. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Backup agents; video streaming; large file upload workflows.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented high-bandwidth hosts with approved outbound patterns.

rules.title: Repeated Denied Outbound Firewall Flows
rules.description: Detects five or more denied outbound firewall flows from the same host in a correlation window. May indicate malware attempting blocked connections. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Misconfigured applications; overly restrictive firewall policy; compliance scanning tools.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known hosts with documented deny-heavy firewall configurations.

rules.title: Unusual Firewall Destination Port Detected
rules.description: Detects outbound connections to known attack framework or backdoor ports (4444, 1337, 31337, etc.). Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate custom application ports; penetration testing infrastructure.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for authorized pen-test infrastructure with documented port usage.

rules.title: Rare External Firewall Destination Detected
rules.description: Detects outbound connections to external IP addresses that are rare or first-seen in the environment. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: New CDN endpoints; cloud service scale-out; new SaaS onboarding.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented new service rollouts with expected new external IPs.

rules.title: Suspicious Allow After Prior Deny on Same Destination
rules.description: Detects a destination IP that was first denied then allowed in the same correlation window. May indicate firewall policy bypass or allow-rule manipulation. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Dynamic firewall rule updates during normal operations; application retry logic.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for destinations with documented dynamic allow-list management.

rules.title: Unusual Login Time (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects login activity outside the entity baseline active-hours window. Uses rolling 30-day behavioral baseline and robust z-score scoring. Advisory-only — no automated account action.
rules.false_positive_notes: Shift workers, employees traveling across time zones, legitimate after-hours access.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for entities with documented irregular schedules or global team membership.

rules.title: Unusual Source IP Diversity (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects an entity authenticating from significantly more distinct source IPs than their 30-day behavioral baseline. Indicates potential credential sharing or compromised account usage across multiple locations. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: VPN users, mobile workforce, users traveling between offices, DHCP rotation on large networks.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for entities known to operate across many locations or use rotating VPN exit nodes.

rules.title: Abnormal Failed Login Ratio (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects an entity whose failed-login ratio in the current window significantly exceeds their 30-day behavioral baseline. Scored using robust z-score. Advisory-only — no automated lockout.
rules.false_positive_notes: Password rotation events, new employee onboarding, SSO migration periods.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress during documented password reset campaigns or SSO cutover windows.

rules.title: Unusual SaaS Action Frequency (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects an entity performing SaaS API or admin actions at a rate significantly above their 30-day behavioral baseline. May indicate automated abuse, compromised token usage, or bulk data operations. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Scripted migrations, bulk export jobs, admin automation, new SaaS feature adoption.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for service accounts with documented automation workloads or during bulk migration windows.

rules.title: Unusual Process Execution Frequency (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects a host executing processes at a rate significantly above or below its 30-day behavioral baseline. High frequency may indicate scripted activity or malware; low frequency may indicate a dormant host suddenly activated. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Patch management, scheduled software updates, large build pipelines, CI/CD runners.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known build/CI hosts or during documented patch windows.

rules.title: Abnormal Network Destination Frequency (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects a host contacting significantly more distinct network destinations than its 30-day behavioral baseline. High destination diversity may indicate C2 scanning, beaconing, or lateral movement preparation. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Scheduled network scanners, monitoring agents, CDN-backed applications with many destinations, update services.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known monitoring infrastructure or documented wide-reach application servers.

rules.title: Abnormal Outbound Data Volume (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects a host transmitting outbound data significantly above its 30-day bytes-out behavioral baseline. May indicate data exfiltration, bulk upload, or compromised host. Scored using robust z-score. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Backup jobs, bulk cloud uploads, video conferencing, OS/application update downloads.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for hosts running documented backup or bulk upload workloads during known maintenance windows.

rules.title: Unusual Host Usage Pattern (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects a host showing behavioral finding frequency significantly above its 30-day endpoint activity baseline. May indicate malware execution, persistence staging, or misuse. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Developer workstations during active projects, shared hosts serving multiple users, fresh deployments.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known high-activity developer machines or shared terminal servers.

rules.title: Peer Group Behavior Deviation (UEBA Baseline)
rules.description: Detects an entity whose behavioral baseline metrics deviate significantly from its deterministic peer group (users with same role, hosts with same function). Peer group deviation is scored using group mean and standard deviation. Advisory-only — no automated enforcement.
rules.false_positive_notes: Recently onboarded users whose baseline has not yet stabilized, role transitions, entities with unique legitimate workloads.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for entities in onboarding period (first 14 days) or with documented atypical workflows.

rules.title: Suspicious Interpreter Chain
rules.description: Detects interpreter-to-interpreter chains (Python->bash, bash->curl). Indicates script-driven lateral movement or C2 staging.
rules.false_positive_notes: CI/CD pipelines and dev environments legitimately chain interpreters. Baseline host first.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Privilege Escalation Indicator
rules.description: Detects uid transitions to root, sudo invocations from non-standard processes, and Windows high-integrity process creation.
rules.false_positive_notes: sudo/su usage is common in admin workflows. Correlate with auth events.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Suspicious Persistence Indicator
rules.description: Detects new persistence entries via registry Run keys, cron, or service install. Indicates potential malware or attacker persistence.
rules.false_positive_notes: Installers and updates legitimately modify Run keys and services. Verify signing status.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Abnormal Network Connection
rules.description: Detects outbound connections to rare destinations not seen in the baseline window. May indicate C2 or data exfil staging.
rules.false_positive_notes: Cloud CDNs appear rare without domain whitelisting. Correlate with threat intel.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Suspicious Shell Spawn from Web/Service Process
rules.description: Detects shell spawned by web server, app server, or database process. Indicates web shell, command injection, or RCE.
rules.false_positive_notes: Maintenance scripts and deployment automation may spawn shells from service accounts.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Rare Process Execution
rules.description: Detects processes with low frequency vs behavioral baseline. May indicate malware, LOLBin abuse, or first-time-seen tools.
rules.false_positive_notes: SW updates, package installs, admin tools trigger this. Correlate with change management.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Container Escape Indicator
rules.description: Detects patterns associated with container escape: process outside expected namespace, breakout_indicator activity type.
rules.false_positive_notes: Privileged containers and debug tools trigger this. Verify container security policy.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: Suspicious Script Block Execution
rules.description: Detects PowerShell or interpreter script blocks with encoded or obfuscated content. Indicates malware staging, credential dumping prep, or lateral movement.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate automation, Chocolatey, and installers use encoded PS. Verify hash against known-good baseline.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for 24h after first occurrence on the same host for known-good processes.

rules.title: LSASS Access Indicator (Advisory)
rules.description: Detects process access to lsass.exe memory. Advisory-only indicator of potential credential dumping. No active containment triggered.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate AV/EDR processes, Windows Defender, and debuggers access lsass. Verify process signature and ancestry.
rules.suppression_guidance: Allowlist signed security tool binaries with verified vendor hashes.

rules.title: Token Impersonation Indicator
rules.description: Detects token impersonation or privilege duplication API usage indicating potential credential theft or lateral movement preparation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate software using impersonation for COM server calls. Verify process ancestry and code signing.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known system processes with valid signatures for 8h windows.

rules.title: Abnormal Authentication Chaining
rules.description: Detects rapid successive authentication events across multiple protocols from the same process, indicating credential relay or pass-the-hash activity.
rules.false_positive_notes: SSO clients, VPN software, and domain-join processes can trigger multi-protocol auth chains legitimately.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented SSO client processes with verified authentication scope.

rules.title: Credential Dump Behavioral Indicator
rules.description: Detects behavioral pattern consistent with credential dumping tools: access to SAM/NTDS database files or registry credential hives.
rules.false_positive_notes: Domain backup tools and legitimate AD management utilities access NTDS. Require signed binaries from approved backup vendors.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for backup agents with verified hash allowlists. Review suppression quarterly.

rules.title: Registry Run Key Persistence
rules.description: Detects writes to HKLM/HKCU Run or RunOnce registry keys by non-system processes, indicating persistence installation.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate software installers, update agents, and licensed applications add run key entries during setup.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by registry key value + signed installer hash. Require installer provenance documentation.

rules.title: Startup Folder Persistence
rules.description: Detects file writes to Windows Startup folder or equivalent system startup directories by non-installer processes.
rules.false_positive_notes: Approved enterprise software deployment tools write to startup during provisioning. Verify SCCM/Intune provenance.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress writes from approved deployment tools. Review quarterly.

rules.title: Suspicious Cron Modification
rules.description: Detects modifications to crontab or cron.d directories by non-root, non-admin processes on Linux/Unix endpoints.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate deployment and configuration management tools (Ansible, Chef) modify crontab during provisioning.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented CM tool user accounts. Require signed audit trail.

rules.title: WMI Event Subscription Persistence
rules.description: Detects creation of WMI permanent event subscriptions, a stealthy persistence mechanism used by advanced threat actors.
rules.false_positive_notes: SCCM and some enterprise monitoring tools use WMI subscriptions. Require explicit allowlist entry with documented business justification.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress only for documented SCCM/monitoring subscriptions with named owner.

rules.title: Log Tampering Indicator
rules.description: Detects processes clearing, truncating, or modifying Windows Event Log or syslog files — a defense evasion indicator.
rules.false_positive_notes: Log rotation daemons (logrotate, Windows Task Scheduler log archiving) perform expected log operations.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for known log rotation processes with validated schedule. Never suppress for interactive or shell-invoked processes.

rules.title: AMSI Bypass Indicator (Advisory)
rules.description: Detects behavioral patterns associated with AMSI bypass attempts: memory patching of amsi.dll or known bypass script patterns. Advisory-only.
rules.false_positive_notes: Security testing frameworks and authorized red team tooling. Require documented change request and signed authorization.
rules.suppression_guidance: Never suppress without signed analyst authorization. Review weekly.

rules.title: Obfuscated PowerShell Execution
rules.description: Detects PowerShell invocations with multiple layers of obfuscation — character substitution, backtick escaping, or concatenation bypass patterns.
rules.false_positive_notes: Some enterprise management scripts use encoding for special characters. Validate against known baseline hashes.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress only with documented hash allowlist entry. Review quarterly.

rules.title: Telemetry Disablement Indicator
rules.description: Detects processes stopping or disabling security telemetry agents, audit services, or monitoring daemons.
rules.false_positive_notes: Authorized OS upgrades and agent update procedures may temporarily stop monitoring services.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress only with documented maintenance window and change ticket. Duration must not exceed 2h.

rules.title: Abnormal Remote Execution
rules.description: Detects remote code execution via PsExec, WMI, or remote scheduled tasks originating from non-admin workstations.
rules.false_positive_notes: IT admin tools and endpoint management platforms execute remotely as standard operations.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented IT admin system accounts with change approval workflow.

rules.title: Suspicious SMB Lateral Activity
rules.description: Detects SMB connections from endpoints to multiple targets in a short window, suggesting lateral movement or credential validation sweeps.
rules.false_positive_notes: File servers, backup agents, and print spoolers generate expected SMB fan-out. Baseline by host role.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented file server roles. Threshold-tune per host classification.

rules.title: WinRM Lateral Movement Indicator
rules.description: Detects WinRM/PowerShell remoting usage from workstation endpoints to multiple target hosts, inconsistent with baseline admin patterns.
rules.false_positive_notes: Ansible, DSC, and remote management frameworks use WinRM. Baseline by source host identity.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented automation accounts. Require peer review on suppression decisions.

rules.title: Multi-Host Propagation Chain
rules.description: Detects a coordinated behavioral pattern across 3 or more hosts: same process name, similar execution timing, and shared network indicators.
rules.false_positive_notes: Software patch deployments and configuration pushes exhibit synchronized multi-host execution. Verify against patch management schedule.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress with documented deployment window. Require change management ticket reference.

rules.title: Suspicious Container Exec
rules.description: Detects docker exec or kubectl exec commands launching interactive shells or unexpected binaries inside production containers.
rules.false_positive_notes: Authorized debugging sessions by on-call engineers. Require change ticket and time-bounded suppression.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress for documented on-call debug sessions with explicit duration bound (max 2h).

rules.title: Privileged Container Runtime Anomaly
rules.description: Detects privileged containers executing host-level system calls or accessing host filesystem paths inconsistent with workload profile.
rules.false_positive_notes: Some infrastructure containers (CNI plugins, monitoring agents) legitimately run privileged. Baseline by container image name.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by documented infrastructure container image hash. Review allowlist monthly.

rules.title: Container Escape Indicator
rules.description: Detects behavioral patterns suggesting container escape: namespace breakout signals, cgroup manipulation, or proc filesystem access from within a container context.
rules.false_positive_notes: Extremely rare in legitimate workloads. Any suppression requires CISO sign-off.
rules.suppression_guidance: Never suppress without CISO authorization. Escalate immediately to SOC lead.

rules.title: Abnormal Container Runtime Behavior
rules.description: Detects containers spawning child processes, network listeners, or file system writes outside their expected behavioral baseline.
rules.false_positive_notes: Sidecar containers, init containers, and containers with dynamic config often exhibit unexpected behavior on first run.
rules.suppression_guidance: Suppress by container image baseline profile. Require documented expected behavior spec.
